title: Damson and frangipane tart
subtitle: halved damsons pressed into an almond frangipane filling in a shortcrust case
excerpt: Damson and frangipane tart is a shortcrust pastry case filled with almond frangipane and topped with halved damsons pressed in cut side up. The frangipane rises around the fruit as it bakes, giving a moist almond sponge base with sharp, jammy damsons across the surface. The frangipane keeps the tart moist for two days. Damsons are very sour; the filling absorbs some of the acidity but the fruit stays sharp against the sweet almond base.
sourceNotes: Frangipane tarts with stone fruit are documented in British and French cookbooks from the seventeenth century onward. Damsons are a traditional British wild plum used extensively in September preserving and baking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A baked almond cream filling made from butter, sugar, ground almonds, and eggs. Bakes to a moist, dense sponge inside a pastry case; fruit is pressed in before baking.
Baking a pastry case without filling, using baking paper and baking beans as a weight to keep the pastry flat. Pre-baked until dry before a wet filling is added.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked tart whole, wrapped tightly, for up to 1 month. Thaw overnight at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tart is better the day after baking once the frangipane has settled. Keeps at room temperature, loosely covered, for 2 days.

Make the pastry: rub cold butter into flour and icing sugar until crumbly. Add the egg yolk and bring together into a dough. Press flat, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Roll to about 3 mm and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 20 minutes. Heat the oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Blind-bake with baking paper and baking beans for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 8 minutes until dry and very lightly coloured. Reduce the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4).
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the almond extract. Fold in the ground almonds and flour.
Spread the frangipane evenly over the warm pastry base. Press the halved damsons into the filling, cut side up, spacing them evenly.
Bake at 180 degrees C for 35 to 40 minutes until the frangipane is risen, golden, and set in the centre with no wobble. A skewer inserted into the frangipane (not a damson) should come out clean.
Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before unmoulding. Serve warm or at room temperature with cream or creme fraiche.

attrs.problem: Frangipane sinks in the centre after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven door in the first 25 minutes; a blast of cold air causes the frangipane to sink.
attrs.fix: Check the tart at 35 minutes; the centre should be just set with no wobble. If still liquid in the centre, give it another 5 minutes with a piece of foil over the top to stop the surface browning further.

attrs.problem: Pastry base soggy beneath the frangipane
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the blind-bake or under-baking the pastry case before adding the frangipane.
attrs.fix: The base must be dry and pale golden before the frangipane goes in. Add the frangipane while the pastry is still warm; it helps seal the surface.
